title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #12

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does removing waste mean for a plant? (1 mark)
   A. Sending out roots
   B. Throwing away its seeds
   C. Cutting its own leaves
   D. Getting rid of things its body does not need

2. Which animal group breathes using gills? (1 mark)
   A. Reptiles
   B. Fish
   C. Mammals
   D. Birds

3. Which group of vertebrates has feathers? (1 mark)
   A. Reptiles
   B. Fish
   C. Birds
   D. Amphibians

4. How many legs does a spider have? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Ten
   C. Four
   D. Eight

5. What do teeth do in digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Store waste
   B. Digest food into the blood
   C. Take back water
   D. Cut and grind food into small pieces

6. Which part of the digestive system is the widest tube near the end? (1 mark)
   A. Anus
   B. Gullet
   C. Small intestine
   D. Large intestine

7. What does the small intestine mainly absorb? (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Sound
   C. Air
   D. Digested food

8. What does the stomach do to food? (1 mark)
   A. Churns it and mixes it with juices
   B. Takes back water
   C. Cuts it into pieces
   D. Stores faeces

9. When reading a measuring jug, where should your eye be? (1 mark)
   A. At the same level as the water surface
   B. Far from the jug
   C. Below the jug
   D. Above the jug

10. Which state of matter has no fixed shape and no fixed volume? (1 mark)
   A. Powder
   B. Solid
   C. Gas
   D. Liquid

11. What does a football need to keep its shape? (1 mark)
   A. Sand
   B. Milk
   C. Air
   D. Water

12. Which of these gases do we breathe in to stay alive? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fumes
   B. Dust
   C. Smoke
   D. Oxygen

13. Which disease can spread by mosquitoes breeding in old tins that hold water? (1 mark)
   A. Sunburn
   B. Malaria
   C. Diarrhoea only
   D. Toothache

14. Which of these breaks down and rots easily? (1 mark)
   A. Glass bottle
   B. Tin can
   C. Vegetable peelings
   D. Plastic bag

15. Which of these is needed to harvest rainwater from a roof? (1 mark)
   A. A ladder only
   B. A gutter and a tank
   C. A fan
   D. A torch

16. Why do we need water for farming? (1 mark)
   A. To bake bricks only
   B. To make wind
   C. Crops and livestock need water
   D. To make stones

17. Where should a water conservation poster be put? (1 mark)
   A. Under a bed
   B. In a cupboard
   C. Near a tap or the school gate
   D. In a bin

18. Which of these is NOT an effect of force? (1 mark)
   A. Changing shape
   B. Stopping motion
   C. Starting motion
   D. Making something have colour

19. What does a force do when it squeezes a sponge? (1 mark)
   A. Makes it lighter
   B. Changes its shape
   C. Changes its colour
   D. Makes it hot

20. A stone and a crumpled paper are dropped together. They land almost together because (1 mark)
   A. The stone is lighter
   B. Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
   C. There is no gravity
   D. The paper is heavier

21. How can a farmer keep a wheelbarrow running smoothly? (1 mark)
   A. Add sand to the wheel
   B. Oil its moving joints
   C. Use rough paint
   D. Leave it in the rain

22. Logs placed under a heavy load help it move because they act as (1 mark)
   A. Rollers
   B. Glue
   C. Weights
   D. Brakes

23. Which of these is a torch used for? (1 mark)
   A. To cool a room
   B. To make food
   C. To make sound
   D. To give light in the dark

24. Which artificial light uses energy from the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Firewood
   B. Solar lamp
   C. Candle
   D. Paraffin lamp

25. Which of these makes its own light? (1 mark)
   A. A shiny cup
   B. A mirror
   C. A white wall
   D. A glow-worm

26. What is the purpose of skylights? (1 mark)
   A. Let daylight through the roof
   B. Make the house hot
   C. Let rain in on purpose
   D. Block light

27. Which of these uses of light is for plants? (1 mark)
   A. Making them cold
   B. Making them bend downward
   C. Making their own food
   D. Making roots taller

28. Which of these is a source of heat from burning? (1 mark)
   A. A cup
   B. A ruler
   C. Charcoal
   D. A book

29. Which is a correct statement about heat? (1 mark)
   A. It moves from cold to warm
   B. It has mass
   C. It stays still
   D. It moves from a warm object to a cooler one

30. Why does an ice cube melt in your hand? (1 mark)
   A. Cold goes into your hand
   B. Heat goes from your hand into the ice
   C. The ice makes heat
   D. The hand makes water

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. What is meant by water conservation? (2 marks)

32. A ball is at rest. Kelvin kicks it, then Mercy stops it with her foot, then she kicks it to the right. Name the effect of the force in each case. (3 marks)

33. State three things that plants give to people. (3 marks)

34. Name two things a farmer can do to save water. (2 marks)

35. Explain the difference between reducing and reusing water. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

36. Explain how ball bearings help a bicycle move. (4 marks)

37. A shopkeeper has 2 kg of sugar and 750 g of salt. Find the total mass in grams. (3 marks)

38. Name two roots, two stems and two leaves that people eat. (4 marks)

39. Describe the differences between mammals and birds. (4 marks)

40. State three things a child should do when he has diarrhoea. (3 marks)

41. Describe the methods of conserving water. Include reducing, reusing and recycling with examples. (5 marks)

42. Draw a table with two columns headed vertebrates and invertebrates. Place these animals correctly: goat, butterfly, snake, snail, hen, spider. (5 marks)

43. Explain what would happen to a young bean plant if all its leaves were removed and why. (4 marks)

44. Explain why a rainwater tank should have a lid. (3 marks)

45. Why is chewing food well important? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Getting rid of things its body does not need
   Living things must remove waste made in their bodies.

2. B — Fish
   Fish take oxygen from water with gills.

3. C — Birds
   Only birds have feathers.

4. D — Eight
   Spiders have eight legs.

5. D — Cut and grind food into small pieces
   Chewing makes food smaller.

6. D — Large intestine
   The large intestine is wider than the small intestine.

7. D — Digested food
   Digested food passes through its wall into blood.

8. A — Churns it and mixes it with juices
   The stomach churns food into a thick soup with digestive juices.

9. A — At the same level as the water surface
   This gives an accurate reading.

10. C — Gas
   Gases spread out to fill all the space.

11. C — Air
   The air inside fills the football.

12. D — Oxygen
   Oxygen in the air is needed for life.

13. B — Malaria
   Mosquitoes spread malaria and breed in standing water.

14. C — Vegetable peelings
   Vegetable peelings are decomposable.

15. B — A gutter and a tank
   Gutters carry rain to a tank.

16. C — Crops and livestock need water
   Water is needed for plants and animals.

17. C — Near a tap or the school gate
   Posters should be seen by many people.

18. D — Making something have colour
   Colour is not caused by a force.

19. B — Changes its shape
   Squeezing changes the shape.

20. B — Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
   The air has very little effect on the crumpled paper.

21. B — Oil its moving joints
   Oil reduces friction.

22. A — Rollers
   Rollers reduce friction.

23. D — To give light in the dark
   A torch is an artificial light source.

24. B — Solar lamp
   A solar lamp charges by day.

25. D — A glow-worm
   Glow-worms produce their own light.

26. A — Let daylight through the roof
   Skylights are roof openings or sheets that let light in.

27. C — Making their own food
   Plants use light to make food.

28. C — Charcoal
   Charcoal gives out heat when it burns.

29. D — It moves from a warm object to a cooler one
   Heat moves from hot to cold.

30. B — Heat goes from your hand into the ice
   Heat moves from the warm hand to the ice.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Using water carefully and protecting water sources so that there is enough for everyone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for careful use and 1 mark for protecting or enough for everyone.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kelvin starts motion, Mercy stops motion, Mercy's second kick changes direction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct effect.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Food, shade, wood, medicine, clean air (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Use drip irrigation, use mulch, water at cooler times, harvest rainwater.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reducing means using less water, for example closing the tap. Reusing means using the same water again, for example using washing water for the garden.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for examples.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: They are small steel balls in the wheel. They roll between moving parts, so there is less friction and the wheels turn easily.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what they are, 1 mark for rolling, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for wheels turning easily.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2750 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 2 kg = 2000 g, 1 mark for adding 750 g and 1 mark for the answer.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots: carrot, cassava, sweet potato. Stems: sugarcane. Leaves: cabbage, sukuma wiki, spinach (any two of each, with correct grouping).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair and 1 mark for correct grouping overall.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mammals have hair or fur and feed their young on milk and most give birth to live young. Birds have feathers and wings and lay eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four differences.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tell an adult, drink clean water or ORS, and see a health worker. Keep clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct action.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce wastage: close taps. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants. Recycle: cleaning used water at a treatment plant or filtering. Include rainwater harvesting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three methods, 1 mark for correct examples and 1 mark for harvesting.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Vertebrates: goat, snake, hen. Invertebrates: butterfly, snail, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the table and 4 marks for placing the six animals (award 1 mark for two correct).

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: The plant would become weak and stop growing. Leaves make food for the plant. Roots can take in water but without leaves the plant cannot make enough food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for weak or stops growing, 1 mark for leaves make food, 1 mark for no food made, 1 mark for roots alone are not enough.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps out dirt and leaves and stops mosquitoes from breeding in it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for mosquitoes, 1 mark for making water safer.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: It breaks food into small pieces and makes digestion easier.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for small pieces and 1 mark for easier digestion.
